script: Shaq dunked so hard he changed the NBA. You see old backboards used to just be bolted to a metal plate, causing things like this to happen. It went from an amazing highlight to a huge safety hazard. From college players to Michael Jordan, they were all shattering backboards. But it wasn't just the backboard that was the problem. Players like Shaq were so powerful they brought the entire thing down. This caused every team to start bringing backups in the arena for moments like these or else the game would be cancelled. It happened so often Shaq even has a tree made up of all the rims he's broken, which forced the league to change how they made them, creating the Shaq proof breakaway rim attached to the arm. Sports Science would test the new rim with NBA center Amar'e Stoudemire. He was brought in to dunk with as much strength as he could, with his best attempt being a thousand pounds of force, and the backboard remained intact. They even went as far as dropping a piano right on the rim with 6,000 pounds of force and still the backboard didn't shatter. Since then, no NBA player has come close to breaking the backboard on the modern NBA hoop.
what_makes_it_work: Strong narrative hook connecting Shaquille O'Neal's physical dominance directly to an NBA equipment redesign.
Visually engaging mix of viral destruction clips, 3D technical animations, and extreme test footage like dropping a piano on a basketball hoop.
Clear, concise explanation that turns basketball history into an entertaining science and engineering story.
